notes:
Summary: Cobalt builds an IDE copilot optimized for in-editor completions and refactors. Primary constraint = TTFT and jitter in VSCode extension over SSH + remote dev containers. Wants to avoid full model shipping to user machines; prefers private VPC control plane with on-prem inference option for enterprise customers.

Key ask from initial call:
- TTFT target: 60-120ms in NA; P95 < 250ms, P99 < 400ms.
- Streaming behavior: incremental token deltas, want deterministic first-token arrival for UI placeholder.
- Token budget per completion: default 64 tokens, but variable for multi-line refactor (up to 256 tokens) with dynamic budget fallback.
- Backpressure: client-side NACK + hinting to throttle editor when host CPU spikes. Concerned about editor UI jitter during batched responses.
- Model/version pinning: need stable pinned model for QA (code-stable-2024-10) + automatic read-only fallbacks to a smaller quantized model for degraded modes.

Quoted from lead engineer: "If the first token shows after 120ms the editor feels laggy — users bounce. We need near-instant first byte plus smooth continuation."

Technical notes captured during demo:
- Prototype using hosted API: streaming frames of 16 tokens every 40ms -> observed TTFT ~140ms due to network and cold-start hashing.
- Suggested changes from Redwood SE: reduce initial frame to 1-2 tokens (first-byte), then 8-token frames; enable prefix KV caching for repeated file headers; shorter batching window (1-3ms) for IDE endpoint.
- Token budgeting: propose token-credit buckets per editor session (e.g., 1k tokens/min quota) + dynamic refill. POC should test 64/128/256 budgets.
- Backpressure pattern: client sends observed latency metric; server uses adaptive batching and signals with X-Backpressure headers. If editor reports CPU > 75% -> server drops batch window to 0 and streams single-token frames.
- Fallback routing: prefer redwood-code-13b-quant (fast) for streaming; fallback to redwood-code-7b for emergency in EU region.

Security/compliance:
- Must support SSO (SAML) and AD group sync for rollout gating.
- Audit logs required for all code completions (retention 90 days).
- KMS integration for CI secrets.

Business context:
- Product is commercializing an enterprise edition; willing to pay for dedicated capacity if latency SLOs are met. Benchmarking and a security pack will influence procurement.

Notes for Redwood sales/engineer:
- Run a 48-hour POC of dedicated vs hosted streams, capture TTFT, P50/P95/P99, jitter (ms variance), and token spend per session.
- Provide a configuration template: streaming_frame_sizes, initial_frame_tokens, batching_window_ms, backpressure_thresholds, token_budget_policy.
- Shipping a short latency digest for execs (one pager) + an answers doc for SAML mapping.

Short next steps (from call):
- SE to schedule POC perf plan (Marco).
- Security kickoff with Redwood security (Aisha to introduce) next week.
- Cobalt to provide representative extension telemetry and a small synthetic load harness.

Staging: close looks achievable Q1 2025 if POC passes.
